hints: Look carefully at what each letter in the Venn means, A is only cartilage plus cilia, C is only cilia plus goblet cells, D is only cartilage plus goblet cells, and B is the middle where all three overlap.
Recall the lining of the trachea for gas exchange protection, what keeps it open, what sweeps mucus up, and what makes the mucus in the first place.
walkthrough:
**Read the Venn diagram**

Think of each circle as a yes for that tissue. You need the region that says yes to all three tissues found in the trachea.

Region B is the centre where cartilage, cilia and goblet cells all overlap.

**Recall trachea structure**

The trachea is held open by C-shaped rings of cartilage so air can always flow. It is lined by ciliated epithelium with goblet cells between the ciliated cells.

Goblet cells secrete mucus to trap dust and microbes, and cilia beat to sweep that mucus up to the throat.

**Pick the matching region**

Since the trachea contains cartilage AND cilia AND goblet cells, you need all three circles together. That is only region B in the very middle.

options.A: Region A is cartilage plus cilia only, with no goblet cells. The trachea does have goblet cells to make mucus, so this is incomplete.
options.B: Region B is the overlap of all three circles. This is correct because the trachea has cartilage for support, cilia for moving mucus, and goblet cells for secreting mucus.
options.C: Region C is cilia plus goblet cells only, with no cartilage. The trachea must have cartilage rings to prevent collapse, so this is incomplete.
options.D: Region D is cartilage plus goblet cells only, with no cilia. The trachea must have cilia to move mucus away from the lungs, so this is incomplete.
